issues.legal_issue: A tenant’s failure to pay rent is not wilful when the tenant genuinely believed, on the basis of a prior purchase agreement and earnest money paid, that there was no obligation to pay rent.
material_facts: The tenant did not pay rent for the period claimed by the landlords.
The tenant asserted that the former owners had orally agreed to sell the property to him before selling it to the landlords.
The tenant had paid earnest money under the asserted agreement and genuinely believed he was entitled to purchase the property and was not obliged to pay rent.
The tenant’s suit for specific performance had been dismissed, but an appeal was pending.
issues.conclusion: The default was not wilful. The tenant was entitled to a reasonable opportunity to pay the arrears, so the eviction decree was set aside and the matter was remitted to the Controller to give him that opportunity.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 10(2)(i) of the Andhra Pradesh Buildings (Lease, Rent and Eviction) Control Act, 1960, read with its proviso, a tenant whose rent default is not wilful may be given a reasonable time to pay or tender the arrears, and the eviction application must be rejected if payment or tender is made within that time. A default is wilful only if it is intentional, deliberate, calculated and conscious, with full knowledge of its legal consequences. The Court relied on S. Sundaram Pillai v. V.R. Pattabiraman, which considered the meaning of “wilful default.”

rule.if: tenant_eviction_for_rent_default and rent_not_paid and bona_fide_belief_of_purchase_right and earnest_money_paid and believed_no_rent_obligation

predicates.tenant_eviction_for_rent_default: A landlord sought to evict a tenant on the ground that rent had not been paid.
predicates.rent_not_paid: The tenant did not pay or tender the rent claimed by the landlord.
predicates.bona_fide_belief_of_purchase_right: The tenant genuinely believed that a prior agreement gave the tenant a right to purchase the property.
predicates.earnest_money_paid: The tenant had paid earnest money under the asserted purchase agreement.
predicates.believed_no_rent_obligation: The tenant genuinely believed that the asserted right to purchase meant the tenant was not obliged to pay rent.

issues.definition: When a landlord seeks eviction for unpaid rent and the tenant did not pay because the tenant genuinely believed, based on a purchase right supported by earnest money, that no rent was due, the tenant must receive an opportunity to pay the arrears.
